implementation_notes: Use a `#courses` private field (ES2022) and a getter that returns `[...this.#courses]`, `this.#courses.slice()` or a frozen copy. MDN is explicit that the privacy of private elements 'is enforced by JavaScript itself' and that they cannot be reached by property access, Object.keys or even Object.freeze - unlike the old `_courses` convention or a TypeScript `private` that is erased before runtime. When callers only need traversal of a large collection, implement `[Symbol.iterator]()` and yield from the private field instead of copying; when the getter must return a snapshot that can never change, spread into a new array and `Object.freeze` the copy (freezing the internal array instead freezes the owner's own ability to mutate it). A getter with no setter is read-only for assignment, which is the other half of the contract.
pitfalls: `get courses() { return this.#courses; }` re-exposes the live array - the field is private but membership is public again.

Object.freeze on the internal array makes the owner's own push/splice fail silently in sloppy mode and throw in modules/strict mode; freeze the returned copy, or freeze deliberately and switch the owner to immutable updates.
Array copies are shallow: `person.courses[0].name = 'x'` still mutates the shared element object.
Private #elements are not inherited by subclasses, so a subclass cannot reach the collection: expose protected hooks in the base class instead of widening the field.
Returning a copy on every read costs an allocation - for read-heavy hot paths expose an iterator instead of the array.
